description: An IP litigation director must approve the company's response to a competitor's trademark application and finalize the opposition scope, evidence package, and conflict safeguards, with input from trademark counsel, an investigations associate, a brand liaison, and conflicts counsel.

shared_context.S1: A competitor has applied to register the mark "NEXORA" in classes 9 and 42, covering medical diagnostic devices and software-related services.
shared_context.S2: The company owns an earlier NEXORA registration that also covers classes 9 and 42.
shared_context.S3: The competitor has begun marketing products under the mark, and the business team wants a response that protects the company's commercial position without unnecessary disruption.
shared_context.S4: Elena Ward has final authority over the enforcement strategy and the filing package.
shared_context.S5: The firm's standard pre-filing conference requires the responsible trademark, investigations, brand, and conflicts reviewers to report their findings before Elena approves the response.

PF1.text: While reviewing the historical trademark file, Noah found an executed 2019 coexistence letter that permits the competitor's class 42 software use but allows the company to challenge the competitor's class 9 medical-device use; the letter was scanned into an archive folder but not added to the current enforcement file.

PF2.text: Maya's review of customer-support records confirmed exactly 14 documented instances in which customers confused the competitor's medical-device product with the company's product; she has not yet attached the records to the draft filing because her evidence index is still being finalized.

PF3.text: In a direct call this week, the client instructed Sofia that protecting the NEXORA mark for medical devices is the priority and that the client wants to preserve the competitor's permitted software use rather than challenge class 42; this instruction has not yet been entered into the matter-management notes.

PF4.text: Daniel confirmed through the firm's conflicts database that the competitor's parent company is an existing client of the firm in an unrelated tax matter; the firm may proceed only after the competitor-matter team obtains the parent's informed written consent and establishes an ethical screen, and Daniel has not yet placed that result in the filing checklist.

acceptance_conditions: The opposition scope must contain only class 9 and not class 42.
The settlement must preserve the competitor's permitted class 42 software use.
The filing must identify exactly 14 documented customer-confusion incidents.
The settlement must include a conflicts-clearance commitment requiring informed written consent from the competitor's parent before filing.
The settlement must include a conflicts-clearance commitment requiring establishment of an ethical screen before filing.
The settlement must include an evidence-finalization commitment covering the 14 documented incidents.

content_checks.C2: len(decisions['opposition_classes']) == 1 and (9 in decisions['opposition_classes'] or '9' in decisions['opposition_classes'])
content_checks.C3: decisions['class_42_consent'] == True or decisions['class_42_consent'] == 'true' or decisions['class_42_consent'] == 'preserved' or decisions['class_42_consent'] == 'preserve'
content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] == 'conflicts_clearance' or c['type'] == 'condition_precedent' or c['type'] == 'conflicts' or c['type'] == 'conflicts_requirement' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'conflicts_clearance' or c['type'] == 'condition_precedent' or c['type'] == 'conflicts' or c['type'] == 'conflicts_requirement' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'evidence_appendix' or c['type'] == 'evidence_finalization' or c['type'] == 'evidence_completion' or c['type'] == 'evidence' or c['type'] == 'investigations' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The 2019 coexistence letter changes the permissible opposition scope from classes 9 and 42 to class 9 alone and changes the class 42 treatment to preserving the competitor's software use.
The customer-support review changes the evidence count from unspecified to exactly 14 incidents and requires an evidence-finalization commitment covering those records.
The client's instruction changes the commercial scope to protecting medical-device use in class 9 while preserving the competitor's permitted software use in class 42.
The conflicts result changes the filing plan from proceeding without a special condition to requiring both the parent's informed written consent and an established ethical screen before filing.
